([[Raleigh, North Carolina]]) | college = * [[Houston Baptist Huskies men's basketball|Houston Baptist]] (2017–2020) * [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = 2021 | team1 = [[VfL Kirchheim Knights|Kirchheim Knights]] | years2 = 2021–2023 | team2 = [[BC Kolín]] | years3 = 2023–2024 | team3 = [[Caledonia Gladiators]] | years4 = 2024–2025 | team4 = [[Manchester Basketball]] | years5 = 2025–present | team5 = [[Bakken Bears]] | highlights = * 2x Second-team All-[[Southland Conference|Southland]] (2019, 2020) }} '''Ian Rogers DuBose''' (born January 16, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Bakken Bears]] of the [[Basketligaen]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Baptist Huskies men's basketball|Houston Baptist Huskies]] and the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]]. ==Early life== DuBose attended the [[Ravenscroft School]], where he was a member of the [[National Honor Society]]. He averaged 15 points and 2.6 assists per game as a junior.{{cite web |title=Ian DuBose ‘17 Recruiting Profile |url=https://www.ncsasports.org/mens-basketball-recruiting/north-carolina/raleigh/ravenscroft-school/ian-dubose1 |website=NCSA Sports |access-date=October 26, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 20.4 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 5.4 assists per game. DuBose was lightly recruited by major programs, generally considered a backup option in case their top prospect signed elsewhere. However, he was considered the top option by [[Houston Baptist Huskies men's basketball|Houston Baptist]] and he committed to the Huskies in October 2019.{{cite news |last1=Shanahan |first1=Tom |title=Ravenscroft's Ian DuBose going to Houston Baptist |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/high-school/article133351859.html |access-date=October 26, 2021 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=February 17, 2017}} ==College career== DuBose started every game as a freshman, averaging 12.5 points and 5.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Dean |first1=Richard |title=2018-19 Houston Baptist MBB Season Preview |url=https://www.texasbasketball.com/article/2018/10/16/2018-19-houston-baptist-mbb-season-preview?ref=article_preview_title |website=Texas Basketball |access-date=October 26, 2021 |date=October 11, 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} DuBose averaged 17 points, 5.9 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.6 steals per game as a sophomore, shooting 43.8 percent from three-point range. He was named to the Second Team All-[[Southland Conference|Southland]].{{cite news |last1=Dean |first1=Richard |title=Former Houston Baptist star Ian DuBose finds portal to Power Five |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Former-Houston-Baptist-star-Ian-DuBose-picks-Wake-15195847.php |access-date=October 26, 2021 |work=[[Houston Chronicle]] |date=April 12, 2020}} On January 2, 2020 he scored a career-high 44 points and had 11 rebounds in a 111–107 overtime win against [[Central Arkansas Bears basketball|Central Arkansas]].{{cite news |title=DuBose's career high helps Houston Baptist past C. Arkansas |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2020/01/02/duboses-career-high-helps-houston-baptist-past-c-arkansas/40935691/ |access-date=October 26, 2021 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=January 2, 2020}} As a junior, DuBose averaged 19 points, 7.3 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game.{{cite news |last1=Johns |first1=Les |title=BREAKING: HBU grad transfer Ian DuBose commits to Wake Forest |url=https://247sports.com/college/wake-forest/Article/BREAKING-Houston-Baptist-grad-transfer-Ian-DuBose-commits-to-Wake-Forest--145535211/ |access-date=October 26, 2021 |work=247 Sports |date=March 20, 2020}} He was named to the Second Team All-Southland for the second consecutive season and earned Southland men's basketball student-athlete of the year honors with a 3.84 grade point average.{{cite press release|url= https://www.southland.org/news/2020/3/9/sfas-kevon-harris-named-southland-mens-basketball-player-of-the-year.aspx|title= SFA's Kevon Harris named Southland men's basketball Player of the Year|publisher=[[Southland Conference]] |date=March 9, 2020 |access-date=March 9, 2020}} DuBose opted to transfer to [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] as a graduate transfer, choosing the Demon Deacons over offers from [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]], [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].{{cite news |title=Wake Forest adds Ian DuBose, Isaiah Wilkins as transfer help |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29045329/wake-forest-adds-ian-dubose-isaiah-wilkins-transfer-help |access-date=October 26, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 16, 2020}} He remained with the program despite the firing of coach [[Danny Manning]] after having a conversation with new coach [[Steve Forbes (basketball)|Steve Forbes]].{{cite news |last1=Joyce |first1=Ethan |title=Wake Forest's Ian DuBose, a former visiting villain at Joel Coliseum, impressing his new basketball coach |url=https://journalnow.com/sports/college/wfu/wake-forests-ian-dubose-a-former-visiting-villain-at-joel-coliseum-impressing-his-new-basketball/article_5b70c4e6-0e51-11eb-8f9d-435d3b2f7acd.html |access-date=October 26, 2021 |work=[[Winston-Salem Journal]] |date=October 14, 2020}} During his senior season, DuBose missed more than two months of gameplay due to a COVID-19 shutdown and an undisclosed medical issue. In 11 games as a senior, he averaged 10.9 points and 4.6 rebounds per game. Following the season, DuBose opted to turn professional rather than take advantage of the additional season of eligibility, granted by the NCAA due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite news |last1=Johns |first1=Les |title=Wake Forest Basketball - Ian DuBose set to turn professional |url=https://247sports.com/college/wake-forest/Article/Wake-Forest-Basketball-Ian-DuBose-set-to-turn-professional--162661731/ |access-date=October 26, 2021 |work=247 Sports |date=March 23, 2021}} ==Professional career== On August 20, 2021, DuBose signed his first professional contract with the [[VfL Kirchheim Knights|Kirchheim Knights]] of the German [[ProA]] league.{{cite web |title=DuBose Signs First Professional Contract with Kirchheim Knights |url=https://godeacs.com/news/2021/8/20/mens-basketball-dubose-signs-first-professional-contract-with-kirchheim-knights.aspx |website=[[Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] |access-date=October 21, 2021 |date=August 20, 2021}} DuBose was selected with the 12th pick of the second round in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (October)|2021 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{cite news |last1=Murray |first1=Chris |title=Two former Nevada basketball players selected in NBA G League draft |url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/two-former-nevada-basketball-players-selected-in-nba-g-league-draft |access-date=October 26, 2021 |work=Nevada Sports Net |date=October 25, 2021}} However, he was waived on October 29.{{cite news |last1=Cohn |first1=Justin A. |title=Mad Ants make roster move |url=https://www.journalgazette.net/blog/mad-antics/20211029/mad-ants-make-roster-move |access-date=November 1, 2021 |work=The Journal Gazette |date=October 29, 2021}} On November 23, DuBose signed with [[BC Kolín]] of the Czech [[National Basketball League (Czech Republic)|National Basketball League]] (NBL).{{cite web |last1=Roopnarine |first1=Surujh |title=Kolin signs Ian DuBose, ex Kirchheim |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Czech-Republic/news/717654/Kolin-signs-Ian-DuBose,-ex-Kirchheim |website=Eurobasket |access-date=December 25, 2021 |date=November 23, 2021}} In 2023, he joined [[Caledonia Gladiators]]. On December 12, 2024, DuBose signed with [[Manchester Basketball]] of the [[Super League Basketball]],{{cite web |title=MCR Land DuBose! |url=https://www.manchester.basketball/news/mcr-land-dubose |website=[[Manchester Basketball]] |access-date=January 10, 2025 |date=December 12, 2024}} On October 10, 2025, he signed with [[Bakken Bears]] of the [[Basketligaen]].{{Cite Instagram |user=bakkenbears_official |postid=DPog9OeEWpC |title=Stærkt Bears-sammenhold sikrer økonomi til ny amerikansk spiller |date=October 10, 2025}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
